analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: almost nothing in futures — the tape has gone quieter, not louder, into CPI. S&P futures drifted from +0.10% to +0.01% and Nasdaq-100 from -0.22% to -0.39% between the 5:36 AM and 7:13 AM ET readings, while the Dow held +0.37%. The most telling move is Nvidia's: the early +1.3% premarket bounce faded to roughly flat by 7 AM ET, even with Mizuho setting a $250 target and Goldman and Bernstein reiterating Buy/Outperform on Monday — the governance discount is not lifting on analyst support alone, and the House Nov 11 reply deadline is tomorrow. Sea Limited is the morning's earnings story and it's genuinely mixed: revenue $8.6B beat the ~$8.08B consensus by a wide margin and Shopee set records, but basic EPS of $0.81 missed the ~$0.97 consensus, so the print cuts both ways; the extra $1B buyback is the offset. Hims & Hers is the cleaner negative: a surprise Q3 loss, gross margin collapsing to 57% from 74%, and a full-year EBITDA guide cut — the GLP-1 margin mix shift is now a numbers story, not just a narrative. Oil is still the second tailwind but it has bounced off its lows (WTI $84.59 at 5:36 AM ET to $85.12 at 7:14 AM ET), so the disinflation help into CPI is slightly less than it looked an hour ago. Signal vs noise: the CPI print at 8:30 AM ET (30 minutes after this brief) and Waller's 0.3% core trigger are the only real signal this morning; NVDA's intraday premarket wiggle, AMD's -0.6% give-back after its best session in six months, and the Anthropic roadshow are noise until the print lands.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures are flat-to-mixed 90 minutes before the open and 30 minutes before October CPI: as of 7:13 AM ET, S&P 500 futures +0.01%, Dow futures +0.37% and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.39%. CPI lands at 8:30 AM ET (5:30 AM PT) — headline +0.3% m/m and core +0.2% expected, with annual core estimated at 2.8% versus 2.6% in September.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape has gone quieter into the print — the S&P drifted from +0.10% to +0.01% since the 5:36 AM ET reading. Everything this morning is positioning for CPI, not trading on it yet.

headlines.headline: Fed Governor Christopher Waller's London speech (carried from the 4 AM brief) still frames the day: he would back a 25bp December hike even if CPI cools, and a 50bp hike 'should be considered' if core CPI rises 0.3% or more. The 2-year yield is at 4.618%, up ~7bp since his remarks, and December-hike pricing jumped toward 99%.
headlines.why_it_matters: One tenth of a point in core CPI now separates a routine 25bp hike from a 50bp one — that is why futures barely moved overnight despite the hawkish tone, and why the print at 8:30 AM ET is the day's only real event.

headlines.headline: Sea Limited reported Q3 2026 results before the open: GAAP revenue $8.6B, up 43.4% YoY and well above the ~$8.08B consensus; net income $502.5M, up 34% and just above the ~$498.9M Visible Alpha estimate; but basic EPS of $0.81 missed the ~$0.97 consensus. Shopee GMV hit $39.7B (+23%), Shopee revenue rose 41.3% to $6.1B, and the board approved an additional $1.0B in share repurchases. The earnings call is at 7:30 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuinely mixed print — a wide revenue beat against an EPS miss — so the reaction hinges on whether investors weight Shopee's record growth or the profitability shortfall; the extra $1B buyback is the offset. Sea closed Monday at $77.96 (+2.9%).

headlines.headline: Hims & Hers reported Q3 after Monday's close: revenue $890.4M, up 49% YoY and roughly in line with the ~$892.5M consensus, but a surprise net loss of $33.0M (-$0.14/share) versus a +$0.06 expected profit, with gross margin contracting to 57% from 74% on international expansion costs and a mix shift toward lower-margin branded GLP-1 offerings. Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $257-277M from $275-325M, and Q4 revenue guidance of $875-895M came in ~7% below consensus. Shares were down ~2-3% after hours Monday and about 1% lower in premarket Tuesday ($22.70 vs Monday's $22.94 close).
headlines.why_it_matters: The GLP-1 margin squeeze is now a numbers story, not just a narrative — revenue is growing ~49% but profitability is going the wrong way, and the guide cut says management expects that to persist.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's early premarket bounce faded: after rising 1.3% in early premarket trading on the Trump 'I believe him' comment about CEO Jensen Huang, NVDA was roughly flat to slightly lower (-0.1%) by ~7 AM ET and the most active premarket name. Analyst support held on Monday — Mizuho set a $250 price target, Goldman reiterated Buy at $300 and Bernstein reiterated Outperform — but the board probe has no published timeline and Huang's reply to the House chairmen is due tomorrow, Nov 11, ahead of a Nov 18 closed-door briefing. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce fading despite three firms holding firm shows the governance discount is not lifting on analyst support alone — the stock is still trading the investigation timeline, not fundamentals, a week after falling 11.58% and 25% below its 52-week high.

headlines.headline: AMD fell about 0.61% in premarket trading after gaining sharply Monday in its best session in six months on fresh support for its AI business. Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform on Nov 9 with a $600 price target. Micron and Marvell were about 1% higher premarket; Intel was down 0.5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A normal give-back after a big day, with an upgrade in the background — the chip tape is pausing with the rest of the market into CPI rather than extending Monday's +6.85% semis surge.

headlines.headline: Oil kept sliding but bounced off its lows: WTI was $85.12 at 7:14 AM ET, down 1.99% on the day, versus $84.59 at 5:36 AM ET; Brent was $90.58 at 4:30 AM ET, down 2.15%, after slipping below $90 for the first time since August. President Trump said military action against Iran was not needed 'at this point' and the war was 'effectively over militarily.' Brent is down nearly 17% over the past week.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cheaper crude is still a tailwind into CPI, but the bounce off the lows trims the disinflation help slightly versus an hour ago; energy names stay under pressure either way.

headlines.headline: Megacaps are drifting slightly higher in premarket: as of ~7:52-7:55 AM ET, AAPL +0.47% ($352.32), META +0.73% ($646.04), AMZN +0.28% ($267.67) and MSFT +0.09% ($545.68) versus Monday's closes, after all four gained 2.4-5.1% in Monday's rally. No fresh company-specific news for the group this morning.
headlines.why_it_matters: A quiet hold of Monday's gains rather than an extension — the megacaps are waiting on CPI like everything else, with META the modest outperformer after its +5.12% Monday.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.32M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, in line), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. Call color: over 60% of new horsepower scheduled for 2027 delivery is contracted (~90% of first-half deliveries); ~$500M order book through 2029; utilization slipped to 92.1% from 94.0%. New filing note: Alps Advisors raised its stake 15.5% in Q3 and now owns ~14.55% of the partnership. Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September. Cross-current today: oil's slide (WTI ~$85.12) pressures energy names broadly, though USAC's compression business is fee-based.

watch_next: 8:30 AM ET (5:30 AM PT) today — October CPI, 30 minutes after this brief: headline +0.3% m/m and core +0.2% expected; a core print of 0.3% or more puts Waller's 50bp December hike on the table, while 0.2% or below likely keeps it at 25bp. No official annual rates for indexes missing October 2025 data.
Sea Limited earnings call at 7:30 AM ET — whether management's tone on Shopee margins and Monee credit quality steadies the stock after the EPS miss.
Whether Nvidia's faded premarket bounce turns into a second leg down — House chairmen's Nov 11 reply deadline is tomorrow; NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17.
